title: If I May But Touch
description: A sun-baked crowd presses in around a solitary figure at midday; close in warm firelight as a trembling hand reaches for the hem of a robe; then a wide gold dawn burst as the woman stands healed, arms lifted to the light - a short illustrated film on Mark 5:27-29, on reaching for Jesus on purpose instead of brushing past Him by accident.

title: The Word, Faith, and Prayer
description: Our founding teaching, on video — the heart behind everything Word and Faith Network does, spoken plainly, person to person.

title: Lay the Debt Down
description: A single thread wound tight, a quiet room, a slow breath releasing. Restrained, muted-grade motion graphics built around one image: forgiveness as finally letting go of what you'd been gripping — without reopening the door.

title: Lay the Debt Down (Morning Light)
description: The same prayer, retold in warm paper-and-cream tones instead of near-black — the coiled thread finally unwinding into a loose, easy ribbon. Release told gently rather than heavy.

title: Steady, Even When the Day Isn't
description: Four small pictures of one truth: a sunrise, a long road with its waypoints, a seed just breaking ground, an anchor resting beneath slow water. Faith that holds even when feeling doesn't.

title: Approved, Not Ashamed & Planted by the Rivers
description: A sermon-summary reflection drawing together two teachings from this week — studying for an audience of One (2 Timothy 2:15) and the tree planted by the rivers of water (Psalm 1:1-3) — told through a quiet study, a planted seed, a steady anchor, and a slow dawn.

title: An Audience of One
description: A hand finally loosening its grip on something it was holding too tight, giving way to a seed breaking quiet ground, and settling into the stillness of an anchor at rest — a visual journey from straining for applause to resting in God's approval alone.

title: Preach to Your Own Soul
description: A six-chapter illustrated short film: a prophet among dead vines at dusk, a man on an ash heap in grey ruins, a king awake on a moonlit Jerusalem rooftop, three men on three peaks at dawn, a modern man at a rain-streaked window, and a hind on the high places at sunrise. Three ruins, one decision - rejoicing was never a reaction; the will moves first.

title: Peace, Be Still
description: A storm-tossed boat at night under lightning and rain, calmed when a figure stands as black clouds split by gold light, resting at last into a rose-gold sunrise at sea - the story of Mark 4:35-41, and what it means to trust the same voice that's still in the boat with you before the waves actually stop.

title: What Holds You
description: A lone traveler drags a boulder across a dusk canyon, kneels exhausted beneath a vast starlit sky, and watches the stone crack open into gold light as dawn breaks and the weight finally lifts - a short visual parable of Psalm 55:22 and Colossians 1:17, on handing the thing you've been secretly dragging to the One who already holds everything together.
